first_cycle: Four academic routes: GCSE Foundation (AQA), GCSE Higher (AQA), IGCSE Extended (Cambridge), A Level AS (Cambridge).
Each academic route receives one original Daily skill check, one Weekly multi-step application and one Exam integrated reasoning draft.

The initial set of 12 original questions has been independently checked and published to the private Supabase bank; newer batches may be released after full mathematical and duplicate validations under owner's approval.
Persist original question source, four unique answer choices, one keyed correct response, clear worked rationale, common wrong-method cues, approximate timing and tier/level/board.
Question-bank multiple choice is currently one mark in the task marking system; full multi-mark rubric functionality needs separate authoring and assessment implementation.
Later cycles should address GCSE Higher/noncalculator, Cambridge IGCSE Core, Pearson IGCSE 4MA1, IB AA/AI SL/HL, Further Maths and TMUA without mixing incompatible syllabuses.

tier_guidance.daily: Single transferable micro-skill plus explanation of working; short, accessible and purposeful, 2–5 minutes

tier_guidance.exam: Integrated multi-step problem; include justification, suitable domain/restrictions and credible distractors; do not falsely label short practice as a full mock

previous_cycle_original_blueprints.objective: §4.5 work/energy/power; §4.4 inclined motion and friction; §4.1 limiting versus nonlimiting friction
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.daily: A maintenance winch exerts a constant 1.2 kN pull while a load travels at 8 m/s in the direction of force. Calculate instantaneous power in kW; explain why kN×m/s produces kW. (2–3 min; 2 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.weekly: A 4 kg parcel is projected UP a 30° rough incline, μ=0.20, g=10. Draw both free-body diagrams for ascent and descent; find acceleration in each phase and justify why friction reverses direction, not gravity. Compare acceleration magnitudes and check signs. (8–10 min; 7 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.exam: A 2 kg inspection cart enters a 30° rough ramp at 12 m/s against a constant 3 N resistance in addition to gravity, g=10. Find maximum distance along ramp using energy; cross-check by F=ma and SUVAT; explain why mechanical energy is not conserved if resistance is omitted. Check s=144/13 m. (10–13 min; 9 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.misconception: Power vs work; friction always set to μR; same friction direction on return; mixing kg and N; 9709 P4 uses g≈10 and paper questions do not use vector notation.

previous_cycle_original_blueprints.objective: §5.1 histogram frequency density; §5.3 dependent sampling and conditional probability; §5.5 normal and continuity-corrected binomial approximation
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.daily: A frequency histogram has a class width 5 with frequency 18 and another width 12 with frequency 24. Determine both frequency densities and which bar is taller; distinguish height from frequency. (2–3 min; 3 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.weekly: A tray contains 5 amber and 7 blue quality seals. Two are sampled without replacement. Construct a tree, find P(second amber | first blue), then find P(exactly one amber) and test whether the two draw-colour events are independent. (7–10 min; 7 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.exam: Fill weights X are modelled N(500,8²) g. Determine the threshold exceeded by 10% of fills. For 100 independent fills, model the number exceeding this threshold as B(100,0.10), then estimate P(at least 15) using a continuity-corrected normal approximation; justify np>5 and n(1−p)>5, and critique independence. Threshold ≈510.3 g. (11–14 min; 10 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.misconception: Frequency density mistaken for frequency; conditional probabilities treated as independent; SD confused with variance; no 14.5 continuity correction; 9709 P5 excludes circular arrangements.

previous_cycle_original_blueprints.objective: §6.1 Poisson counts/interval scaling; §6.3 density and median by integration (not explicit CDF); §6.5 Type I/II error probabilities
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.daily: A detector receives an average of 0.8 alerts per 10 minutes, modelled by Poisson. Find the mean for 30 minutes and the probability of zero alerts; give a reason a fixed-rate assumption may fail. (3–4 min; 3 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.weekly: For a continuous random variable with f(x)=kx for 0≤x≤3 and zero otherwise, normalise f, calculate P(X>2), and find the median by equating an integral to 1/2. Check k=2/9 and median=3/√2. Do not require the named cumulative distribution function. (7–10 min; 8 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.exam: A monitoring system tests H0:λ=2 against H1:λ>2 for a one-hour Poisson count, rejecting when X≥5. Find the actual Type I error probability under λ=2 and Type II error probability when λ=4; discuss whether a nominal 5% claim is justified and how a different threshold changes both risks. (10–14 min; 10 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.misconception: Poisson mean not rescaled with exposure; using f(x) as P(X=x); invoking an explicit CDF not required by 9709 P6; Type II calculated under null instead of stated alternative.

previous_cycle_original_blueprints.objective: §1.1 sampling techniques; §3.2 conditional probability; §5.3 normal-population mean hypothesis test with known/assumed variance
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.daily: A population has strata of sizes 120, 180 and 300. For a stratified sample of 60, allocate sample sizes 12,18,30 and explain why sampling only volunteers is not equivalent to stratification. (3–4 min; 3 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.weekly: A synthetic survey table records use of a repair app by 2 age groups, with unequal group sizes. Compute P(app|older), P(older|app), and overall P(app); explain which conditional probability answers a stated marketing question and why reversing the condition changes the result. (7–9 min; 7 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.exam: A packaging line has known population SD 4 g and a normal output model. Test H0:μ=100 g against H1:μ>100 g using n=25 and sample mean 101.2 g at 5% one-sided significance. Find z=1.5, state the decision in context, and compare with a second independent sample mean 102.0 g (z=2.5). Critique the normal/known-σ assumptions; do not invoke CLT. (10–14 min; 10 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.misconception: Stratified versus quota/opportunity samples; P(A|B) vs P(B|A); non-rejection does not prove H0; 9MA0 §4.1 excludes calculation of discrete E(X),Var(X); CLT is not required.

previous_cycle_original_blueprints.objective: §6.1 units; §8.4 connected particles and resolving forces; §7.4 two-dimensional calculus kinematics
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.daily: Convert 72 km/h to m/s and explain why 72 m/s is incorrect; extend to a 5-second displacement under constant speed. (2–3 min; 3 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.weekly: A 3 kg particle on a smooth 30° plane is linked over a smooth pulley to a hanging 2 kg particle. With g=9.8, draw separate diagrams, show the 2 kg mass descends, and calculate a=0.98 m/s² and tension 17.64 N; check units and force directions. (8–10 min; 8 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.exam: For a robot on a flat plane, r(t)=2t² i+(t³/3−4t) j metres for 0≤t≤4. Find v(t), a(t), when the j-component of velocity is zero, and why the robot is NOT at rest then. Calculate the net displacement over the interval and comment on distance versus displacement. (10–13 min; 9 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.misconception: g default is 9.8 unless specified; mixing total system with individual-body tensions; horizontal velocity nonzero when vertical component is zero; UK 9MA0 explicitly permits i,j and vector calculus.

previous_cycle_original_blueprints.objective: S1 §3.4 dependent sampling; §2.3–2.4 dispersion/skewness/outliers; §4.3 PMCC and interpretation (no significance tests)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.daily: A box contains 4 red and 6 blue tickets. Two are drawn without replacement. Find P(second red | first blue) and explain why the denominator is 9, not 10. (2–4 min; 3 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.weekly: Two newly invented delivery-route data summaries give medians, quartiles and whisker endpoints. Apply an explicitly supplied 1.5×IQR outlier rule, compare spread and possible skewness, and explain why the same mean can mask different reliability. Focus on interpretation, not drawing a box plot as the direct question. (7–10 min; 8 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.exam: For six newly invented paired observations of temperature and machine output, supply Σx, Σy, Σx², Σy², Σxy. Calculate PMCC r from Sxx,Syy,Sxy, interpret its sign and strength, and critique the claim that temperature causes output changes; NO significance test and no reuse of earlier least-squares-regression blueprint. (10–13 min; 9 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.misconception: Treating without-replacement draws as independent; quartiles/outlier threshold misuse; correlation implies causation; S1 does not require PMCC significance tests and histogram drawing is not direct examination focus.

previous_cycle_original_blueprints.objective: S2 §2.2–2.3 continuous PDF/CDF relation; §1.3 Poisson approximation to binomial; §4.6 Poisson-mean hypothesis test
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.daily: A distribution has F(x)=x²/16 for 0≤x≤4, with F(x)=0 below 0 and 1 above 4. Differentiate to obtain f(x), calculate P(1<X≤3), and verify f is nonnegative. (3–5 min; 4 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.weekly: A process tests 200 independent tiny components, each with failure probability 0.012. Use a Poisson approximation with λ=2.4 to estimate P(at most 1 failure), then compare assumptions with the exact binomial model and explain when approximation could be misleading. (7–10 min; 7 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.exam: An instrument produces Poisson counts with claimed mean 3 per shift. A shift records 8. Form H0:λ=3, H1:λ>3; calculate a one-tailed p-value, find a 5% critical threshold using Poisson tails, and interpret in context, explicitly distinguishing observed significance from a change in true mean. (10–14 min; 10 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.misconception: Confusing F and f; endpoint values of a continuous CDF; Poisson λ=np; tail direction and discrete critical region; S2 contains explicit CDF, unlike Cambridge 9709 P6.

previous_cycle_original_blueprints.objective: M1 §2.1–2.2 vectors in a plane; §5.2 equilibrium of a particle; §4.2 changing-force/connected-particle dynamics
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.daily: A drone's constant velocity vector is (3i+4j) m/s. Find speed and unit direction, explaining why a vector cannot be replaced by its magnitude when direction matters. (2–4 min; 3 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.weekly: A 5 kg suspended instrument is held in equilibrium by two taut cables at distinct specified angles to the horizontal. Construct a free-body diagram and solve the two simultaneous component equations for both tensions; verify vertical components sum to mg and both tensions are positive. (8–11 min; 8 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.exam: A 3 kg mass and a 2 kg mass are joined over a smooth pulley. Starting at rest, the 3 kg mass descends 1 m then reaches the floor. Use g=9.8, find initial acceleration 1.96 m/s² and speed²=3.92; after the string goes slack find the further 0.20 m rise of the 2 kg mass, explaining why the first-phase tension equation no longer applies. (11–15 min; 11 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.misconception: Scalar speed substituted for vector velocity; tension direction; incorrectly keeping taut-string constraint after impact; M1 has no Newton coefficient of restitution requirement (that is M2).

previous_cycle_original_blueprints.objective: M2 §2.1–2.3 centre of mass/lamina equilibrium; §4.2 direct impact and restitution; §2.2 composite lamina without integration
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.daily: Two point masses 2 kg at x=1 m and 1 kg at x=4 m lie on a light line. Find the centre of mass x=2 m and explain why it lies nearer the heavier mass. (2–4 min; 3 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.weekly: A 2 kg particle travelling at 5 m/s collides directly with a stationary 1 kg particle. Coefficient of restitution e=0.5. Apply momentum and restitution to find v1=2.5 m/s and v2=5 m/s; calculate kinetic energy loss 6.25 J and justify why momentum, not kinetic energy, is conserved. (8–11 min; 9 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.exam: A uniform 6×4 rectangular lamina has the top-right 2×2 rectangle removed. With origin at bottom-left, compute the remaining centre of mass (2.6,1.8), then discuss the initial clockwise turning moment when suspended from (0,4) and the stable orientation of its centre of mass below the suspension point. No integration. (11–15 min; 10 marks)
previous_cycle_original_blueprints.misconception: Centre of mass uses masses/areas not simple mean of coordinates; coefficient of restitution not 1 unless stated; impact loses kinetic energy; moment direction depends on pivot; M2 is not interchangeable with M1.
